On September 10, DeepSeek introduced V4.1-Flash, a new model with native image understanding. That means it can use a picture as part of what it receives, rather than working only from words. Vercel had made the model available through its AI Gateway a day earlier.

"} EXACT PASSAGE REFERENCES: [P001] DeepSeek’s new model can understand pictures. Whether you see that depends on the app. [P002] On September 10, DeepSeek introduced V4.1-Flash, a new model with native image understanding. That means it can use a picture as part of what it receives, rather than working only from words. Vercel had made the model available through its AI Gateway a day earlier. [P003] A model does the generating behind an app’s interface, and the app maker chooses which model to connect. Picture a photo app: if its maker connects it to V4.1-Flash and passes along the image, the model can consider the picture when it answers. The new ability is underneath; the app’s own update tells you what is available in the tool you use. [P004] One technical change arrives September 14: requests sent under the older deepseek-v4-pro label are scheduled to route to V4.1-Flash until V4.1-Pro launches. For everyday use, the useful question is simpler: can this specific app accept my picture, and what does it say it can do with it? [P005] “DeepSeek’s new model can take pictures into account. Whether that reaches the tool in front of you depends on the model its maker connected behind the interface.” [P006] AI Fundamentals 101: Wrappers, Harnesses, and the Stack explains how the interface you see sits above the model doing the generating.
